problem: VLN agents rely on implicit cross-modal alignment to ground landmark noun phrases in visual observations, and visual grounding remains weak after downstream VLN training, especially for landmarks that are rare in the training data.
motivation: Text-to-image models carry broad visual knowledge, and matching a generated image to an observation is an image-to-image task that may be easier than language grounding. Cognitive science (dual-coding theory, mental imagery) suggests imagery cues help decision making, so the paper asks whether generated landmark images help VLN agents.
key_idea: Generate SDXL images ("imaginations") for landmark-bearing sub-instructions, feed them to existing VLN agents as an extra modality concatenated with the text encodings, and add a cosine alignment loss between each imagination and its noun-phrase embedding.
insight: Gains are modest (about 1 SR) and come from both training and inference. Imaginations removed at test time still beat the baseline (66.92 vs 66.24 SR), suggesting a regularisation effect, while mismatched imaginations drop SR to baseline level (66.24). Imaginations from the full sequence of sub-instructions beat the goal-only imagination (67.26 vs 66.79 SR), and visual imaginations beat textual sub-instruction embeddings (67.26 vs 66.67 SR). Early fusion with the text beats LAD-style late fusion (72.12 vs 71.73 SR), and a simple MLP encoder suffices.
method: Sub-instruction segmentation and filtering: FG-R2R splits instructions into about 3.66 sub-instructions each; spaCy noun-phrase detection plus a manual blacklist (counts, directions, pronouns) drops sub-instructions without visual landmarks.

Imagination generation (R2R-Imagine): SDXL renders each remaining sub-instruction at 1024x1024 with positive prompts (indoor, house, realistic, real estate) and negative prompts (outdoor, text, humans, collage). This gives about 41.5k train imaginations, about 2.96 per instruction.
Imagination encoder: each image goes through an off-the-shelf ViT-B/16, then a type embedding t_Im is added, then a 3-layer MLP (768-512-768, input dropout 0.15) produces h_i.

Early-fusion integration: the imagination embeddings are concatenated with the instruction embeddings before the cross-modal encoder(s). In HAMT they go to the language branch of the cross-modal transformer; in DUET they go to both the coarse-scale and fine-scale cross-modal encoders.

Auxiliary alignment loss: 1 - cosine similarity between h_i and the mean noun-phrase token embedding from the text encoder, added to the base loss with lambda=0.5. InfoNCE gave no significant difference.

Three-stage fine-tuning: start from full base checkpoints and train for 100k iterations on a V100 (batch 8). The first 25% trains only the MLP and type embedding (lr 1e-4). The next 25% trains everything with the base at 1e-6 and imagination modules at 5e-5. The rest trains all parameters at 1e-6.
REVERIE variant: the entire instruction is treated as a single sub-instruction and one imagination is generated.

setting.backbone: HAMT and DUET (fine-tuned from released checkpoints) + SDXL (frozen, offline imagination generation) + ViT-B/16 (frozen, off-the-shelf) + new 3-layer MLP
setting.training_data: R2R train (and REVERIE train) plus about 41.5k SDXL imaginations (R2R-Imagine); base checkpoints from prior work (HAMT with PREVALENT augmentation); no extra environments beyond Matterport3D
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) plus text instruction and generated imagination images
setting.action_space: discrete navigation-graph viewpoints (HAMT) / topological-map node selection (DUET)
setting.privileged: none (imaginations are generated from the instruction text only)

numbers_note: Split for REVERIE is not printed in the table; the intro states val unseen. Baselines (HAMT 66.24/61.51 SR/SPL; DUET 71.52/60.41 SR/SPL on R2R val-unseen; DUET 46.98 SR on REVERIE) are excluded per rules.
results: Adding imaginations improves R2R val-unseen SR by 1.0 for HAMT (66.24 to 67.26) and 0.6 for DUET (71.52 to 72.12), with SPL up to +0.5. On the R2R test set DUET-Imagine gains 2 SR points (69 to 71), and on REVERIE DUET gains 1.3 SR and 0.82 RGS. The gains are small and do not approach environment-scaling methods such as ScaleVLN.
limitations: Gains are modest (about 1 SR), with many ablation differences within noise, and only two base agents were tested.
Imaginations add generation and encoding cost and are not grounded in the actual environment, so personalized or unique landmarks cannot be imagined.
Evaluated only in the simulator on R2R and REVERIE, with no real-robot experiments.
